# Kael

> GPU-accelerated UI framework for native-first desktop apps in Rust. Aims to replace Electron for high-performance desktop apps without bundling Chromium, with WebView islands available when web compatibility is the right tool.

Kael renders via Metal (macOS), DirectX 11 (Windows), Vulkan (Linux). Apps are primarily Rust UI — no HTML/CSS/JS required for native surfaces. Use `webview(id, url)` for deliberate web-standard islands. One binary, native performance, 60fps (up to 120fps on ProMotion displays).

## Quick start

```toml
[dependencies]
kael = "0.3"
```

```rust
use kael::*;
use kael::prelude::*;

struct MyApp { count: i32 }

impl Render for MyApp {
    fn render(&mut self, _window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
        let entity = cx.entity();
        div().size_full().flex().items_center().justify_center()
            .bg(rgb(0x1E1E1E)).text_color(rgb(0xFFFFFF))
            .child(format!("Count: {}", self.count))
            .child(button("inc").label("+1").on_click({
                let entity = entity.clone();
                move |_, _, cx| {
                    entity.update(cx, |this, cx| { this.count += 1; cx.notify(); });
                }
            }))
    }
}

fn main() {
    Application::new().run(|cx: &mut App| {
        let bounds = Bounds::centered(None, size(px(400.0), px(300.0)), cx);
        cx.open_window(
            WindowOptionsBuilder::new().title("My App").windowed(bounds),
            |_, cx| cx.new(|_| MyApp { count: 0 }),
        ).unwrap();
        cx.activate(true);
    });
}
```

## Architecture

- **Application::new().run(|cx| { ... })** — boots platform event loop
- **cx.open_window(options, |window, cx| cx.new(|_| View))** — creates a GPU window
- **Entity<T>** — reactive state container. Read with `.read(cx)`, mutate with `.update(cx, |this, cx| { ... })`
- **cx.notify()** — triggers re-render after state change
- **impl Render for T** — defines how an entity paints itself
- **div()** — base container element, Tailwind-style builder: `.flex()`, `.bg()`, `.text_color()`, `.child()`
- **impl Global for T** — app-wide singleton. Set with `cx.set_global()`, read with `cx.global::<T>()`

## Widget primitives

All widgets: `widget_name(id, value, ...)` → `.on_change(|value, window, cx| { ... })` → `.render_with(|state, ...| { ... })`

| Widget | Constructor | Key props |
|--------|-------------|-----------|
| button | `button(id)` | `.label()`, `.disabled()`, `.on_click()` |
| text_input | `text_input(id, value)` | `.placeholder()`, `.multi_line()`, `.password()`, `.on_change()`, `.on_submit()` |
| checkbox | `checkbox(id, checked)` | `.label()`, `.indeterminate()`, `.on_change()` |
| toggle | `toggle(id, on)` | `.label()`, `.on_change()` |
| radio_group | `radio_group(id, value, options)` | `.on_change()` |
| slider | `slider(id, value)` | `.min()`, `.max()`, `.step()`, `.on_change()` |
| select | `select(id, value, options)` | `.placeholder()`, `.searchable()`, `.on_change()` |
| date_picker | `date_picker(id, date)` | `.on_change()` |
| modal | `modal(id, open)` | `.label()`, `.backdrop()`, `.dismiss_on_escape()`, `.on_change()` |
| popover | `popover(id)` | `.anchor()`, `.popup()`, `.dismiss_on_escape()` |
| tabs | `tabs(id, value, items)` | `.on_change()` |
| disclosure | `disclosure(id, open)` | `.trigger()`, `.panel()`, `.on_change()` |
| progress | `progress(id, value)` | `.indeterminate()` |
| toast | `Toast::new(title)` | `.body()`, `.duration()`, `.position()` |
| splitter | `splitter(id, ratio)` | `.on_change()` |
| label | `label(text, target_id)` | links to control |
| rich_text | `rich_text()` | `.text()`, `.styled(t, HighlightStyle)`, `.link()`, `.mention()`, `.hashtag()`, `.code()` |
| uniform_list | `uniform_list(id, count, renderer)` | `.track_scroll()` |
| recycling_list | `recycling_list(id, count, renderer)` | variable heights |
| sortable_list | `sortable_list(id, count, renderer)` | `.on_reorder()` |
| canvas | `canvas(prepaint_fn, paint_fn)` | custom GPU drawing |
| svg | `svg()` | `.path()`, `.size()`, `.text_color()` |
| lottie | `lottie(source)` | `.autoplay()`, `.loop_forever()`, `.ping_pong()` |

## Electron-gap guidance

- Prefer native Kael UI for app chrome, dashboards, tools, editors, panes, and controls.
- Use `webview(id, url)` plus `webview_controller(id)` for small embeds; use `webview_file(id, path)?` / `webview_file_with_options(id, path, options)?` for Electron-style local `loadFile` islands, and `webview_html(id, html)` / `webview_html_with_options(id, html, options)` for true inline `loadHTML` islands; prefer `webview_with_options(id, url, WebViewOptions::auth_flow(storage_key))` for OAuth/SSO/account pages, `WebViewOptions::embedded_widget()` for payments/maps/docs/customer widgets, and `WebViewOptions::web_graphics()` for browser-only WebGL/WebGPU/canvas islands; add `.devtools()` while developing WebView islands; use `.on_console_message(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.console_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, tests, or agents should receive hosted-page console output and uncaught errors; use `.zoom_hotkeys()` or `.zoom_hotkeys_enabled(true)` when browser content should own zoom shortcuts/gestures; use `.on_keyboard_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.keyboard_event_bridge(kind)` when native chrome should observe hosted keydown, keyup, and beforeinput activity for shortcut coordination or tests; use `.on_location_changed(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.location_bridge(kind)` when native tabs, breadcrumbs, Back/Forward chrome, or agents should observe hosted SPA route changes; use `.on_lifecycle_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.lifecycle_bridge(kind)` when native chrome, resource throttling, tests, or agents should observe hosted focus, visibility, page show/hide, and browser fullscreen changes; use `.on_scroll_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.scroll_bridge(kind)` when native progress, sticky chrome, scroll restoration, tests, or agents should observe hosted scroll and viewport state; use `.on_selection_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.selection_bridge(kind)` when native edit menus, formatting chrome, tests, or agents should observe hosted selection state; use `.media_autoplay()` or `.media_autoplay_enabled(...)` for browser-media islands that need explicit autoplay policy; use `.on_media_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` when native chrome should receive browser audio/video play, pause, seek, time, volume, rate, buffering, metadata, and error events; use `.on_context_menu(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` when native chrome should own right-click or secondary-click menus for hosted WebView content with selected text, link, image, media, editable, and input context; use `.on_pointer_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.pointer_bridge(kind)` when native status bars, hover previews, click handling, tests, or agents need lightweight link/image/media/editable context for hosted content; use `.on_form_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.form_bridge(kind)` when native validation, progress chrome, tests, or agents should observe hosted submit, reset, change, and input activity without bespoke page JavaScript; use `.on_file_input_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.file_input_bridge(kind)` when native upload chrome, tests, or agents should observe browser file-input selections with file names, sizes, MIME types, and last-modified timestamps; use `.on_resource_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.resource_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, loading UI, tests, or agents should observe hosted subresource timing plus element load/error activity without request interception; use `.on_network_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.network_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, loading UI, tests, or agents should observe hosted fetch/XHR outcomes without opening devtools; use `.on_dialog_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.dialog_bridge(kind)` when native diagnostics, tests, or agents should observe hosted alert, confirm, prompt, and beforeunload activity while preserving browser behavior; use `.on_clipboard_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.clipboard_event_bridge(kind)` when native editor chrome, tests, or agents should observe hosted copy/cut/paste events and browser-exposed clipboard data; use `.on_permission_request(kind, |request, window, cx| ...)` or `.permission_bridge(kind)` when native app policy should preflight hosted camera, microphone, display-capture, geolocation, or notification requests before browser prompts continue; use `.on_storage_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.storage_bridge(kind)` when native account chrome, settings sync, tests, or agents should observe hosted localStorage/sessionStorage changes without polling JavaScript; use controller `select_media_text_track(window, selector)` and `disable_media_text_tracks(window)` for browser text tracks; use controller `request_media_fullscreen(window)`, `exit_media_fullscreen(window)`, `request_media_picture_in_picture(window)`, and `exit_media_picture_in_picture(window)` for WebView-hosted video fullscreen/PiP requests subject to browser support and user-gesture policy; use `.background_color(color)` or `.transparent_background()` when an embed should inherit native chrome instead of showing the default WebView rectangle; use `.focused()` or `.focused_enabled(...)` when auth, checkout, editor, or browser-widget islands should take keyboard focus immediately on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; use `.clipboard_access()` or `.clipboard_access_enabled(...)` when hosted rich editors, docs widgets, or browser pages need JavaScript clipboard APIs; use `.javascript_disabled()` or `.javascript_disabled_enabled(...)` for untrusted static docs or previews that should not run page scripts; use `.general_autofill_enabled(false)` or `.general_autofill_disabled()` for Windows/WebView2 general form suggestions, and choose popup behavior with `.deny_new_windows()`, `.open_new_windows_in_current_webview()`, `.allow_new_windows()`, or `.on_new_window(...)` returning `WebViewNewWindowPolicy::{Deny, NavigateCurrent, Allow}`; Linux/Windows honor all policies, while Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honors `Deny`, `NavigateCurrent`, and `Allow` for target-blank requests; macOS `Allow` creates a WebKit-managed popup child WebView inside the same native window, so prefer `NavigateCurrent` or a custom handler when app-owned route/chrome/lifecycle matters; choose download behavior with `.allow_downloads()`, `.deny_downloads()`, `.on_download_started(...)` returning `WebViewDownloadPolicy::{Allow, Deny, SaveTo(path)}`, and `.on_download_completed(...)` for completion handoff; use controller `trigger_download(window, url, filename, callback)` or `download_url(window, url, filename, callback)` for native Save link/image/media commands based on context-menu or pointer bridge URLs; use `.on_document_title_changed(...)` to sync hosted page titles into native window titles, tabs, breadcrumbs, or labels; use `.on_favicon_changed(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` or `.favicon_bridge(kind)` when hosted pages should drive native tab icons, breadcrumbs, history rows, or app switchers; use `.on_page_load(...)` with `WebViewPageLoadEvent::{Started, Finished}` for loading spinners, ready coordination, and auth-flow progress; use `.on_location_changed(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for event-driven hosted SPA URL/title/readyState and Back/Forward chrome sync, and `.on_lifecycle_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for hosted focus/visibility/pagehide/pageshow/fullscreen sync, and `.on_scroll_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for hosted scroll/viewport progress sync, and `.on_selection_event(kind, |event, window, cx| ...)` for hosted selected text/HTML sync on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; use `.on_drag_drop(...)` returning `WebViewDragDropPolicy::{AllowBrowserDefault, BlockBrowserDefault}` or `.block_drag_drop()` when hosted content can receive local file drops and the app must preserve or block browser defaults explicitly. Refine options with `.storage_key(...)`, `.html(...)`, `.clear_html(...)`, `.user_agent(...)`, `.inject_css(...)`, `.inject_javascript(...)`, `.bridge_script()`, `.console_bridge(kind)`, `.on_console_message(kind, handler)`, `.zoom_hotkeys()`, `.zoom_hotkeys_enabled(...)`, `.find_result_bridge(kind)`, `.on_find_result(kind, handler)`, `.keyboard_event_bridge(kind)`, `.on_keyboard_event(kind, handler)`, `.media_autoplay()`, `.media_autoplay_enabled(...)`, `.media_event_bridge(kind)`, `.on_media_event(kind, handler)`, `.context_menu_bridge(kind)`, `.on_context_menu(kind, handler)`, `.pointer_bridge(kind)`, `.on_pointer_event(kind, handler)`, `.form_bridge(kind)`, `.on_form_event(kind, handler)`, `.file_input_bridge(kind)`, `.on_file_input_event(kind, handler)`, `.resource_bridge(kind)`, `.on_resource_event(kind, handler)`, `.network_bridge(kind)`, `.on_network_event(kind, handler)`, `.dialog_bridge(kind)`, `.on_dialog_event(kind, handler)`, `.clipboard_event_bridge(kind)`, `.on_clipboard_event(kind, handler)`, `.permission_bridge(kind)`, `.on_permission_request(kind, handler)`, `.storage_bridge(kind)`, `.on_storage_event(kind, handler)`, `.navigation_state_bridge()`, `.location_bridge(kind)`, `.on_location_changed(kind, handler)`, `.lifecycle_bridge(kind)`, `.on_lifecycle_event(kind, handler)`, `.scroll_bridge(kind)`, `.on_scroll_event(kind, handler)`, `.selection_bridge(kind)`, `.on_selection_event(kind, handler)`, `.background_color(color)`, `.transparent_background()`, `.focused()`, `.focused_enabled(...)`, `.clipboard_access()`, `.clipboard_access_enabled(...)`, `.javascript_disabled()`, `.javascript_disabled_enabled(...)`, `.general_autofill_enabled(...)`, `.general_autofill_disabled()`, `.request_headers(headers)`, `.clear_request_headers()`, `.on_bridge_message(...)`, `.on_message(...)`, `.on_navigate(...)`, `.on_new_window(...)`, `.deny_new_windows()`, `.open_new_windows_in_current_webview()`, `.allow_new_windows()`, `.allow_downloads()`, `.deny_downloads()`, `.on_download_started(...)`, `.on_download_completed(...)`, `.favicon_bridge(kind)`, `.on_favicon_changed(kind, handler)`, `.on_document_title_changed(...)`, `.on_page_load(...)`, `.on_drag_drop(...)`, `.block_drag_drop()`, and `.allow_navigation_schemes(...)`; keep the controller handle for `navigate`, `navigate_with_headers(window, url, headers)`, `load_html(window, html)`, `cookies(window, callback)`, `cookies_for_url(window, url, callback)`, `set_cookie(window, cookie, callback)`, `delete_cookie(window, cookie, callback)`, `url(window, callback)`, `title(window, callback)`, `user_agent(window, callback)`, `is_loading(window, callback)`, `can_go_back(window, callback)`, `can_go_forward(window, callback)` (reads `.navigation_state_bridge()` markers for app-owned same-document Forward buttons), `viewport_snapshot(window, callback)`, `scroll_to(window, x, y, callback)`, `scroll_by(window, dx, dy, callback)`, `scroll_selector_into_view(window, selector, callback)`, `insert_css(window, key, css)`, `remove_inserted_css(window, key)`, `evaluate_javascript`, `evaluate_javascript_with_result(window, script, callback)`, `post_bridge_message(WebViewBridgeMessage::new(kind).with_id(id))`, `respond_to_bridge_message(window, &message, payload)`, `reject_bridge_message(window, &message, reason)`, `post_message`, `reload`, `stop_loading(window)`, `play_media(window)`, `pause_media(window)`, `set_media_muted(window, muted)`, `set_media_volume(window, volume)`, `set_media_playback_rate(window, rate)`, `seek_media_secs(window, seconds)`, `media_command(window, selector, command, callback)`, `set_media_source(window, selector, source, callback)`, `set_media_options(window, selector, options, callback)`, `capture_media_frame(window, selector, options, callback)`, `add_media_text_track(window, selector, track, callback)`, `remove_media_text_track(window, selector, track_selector, callback)`, `select_media_text_track(window, selector)`, `disable_media_text_tracks(window)`, `request_media_fullscreen(window)`, `exit_media_fullscreen(window)`, `request_media_picture_in_picture(window)`, `exit_media_picture_in_picture(window)`, `media_state(window, callback)` (includes fullscreen, picture-in-picture, text tracks, and active cue text), `mute_media(window)`, `unmute_media(window)`, `go_back`, `go_forward`, `open_devtools(window)`, `close_devtools(window)`, `is_devtools_open(window, callback)`, `focus(window)`, `focus_parent(window)`, `set_zoom_factor(window, factor)`, `find_text(window, query, WebViewFindOptions::forward(), callback)`, `find_text_result(window, query, WebViewFindOptions::forward(), callback)` for `WebViewFindResult { found, matches }`, `.find_result_bridge(kind)` / `.on_find_result(kind, handler)` for Electron-style `found-in-page` updates with query, options, found flag, match count, selected text, and URL, `stop_finding(window)`, `stop_finding_with_action(window, WebViewStopFindAction::KeepSelection)`, `copy(window, callback)`, `cut(window, callback)`, `paste(window, callback)`, `select_all(window, callback)`, `undo(window, callback)`, `redo(window, callback)`, `delete_selection(window, callback)`, `insert_text(window, text, callback)`, `focus_selector(window, selector, callback)`, `click_selector(window, selector, callback)`, `add_class(window, selector, class_name, callback)`, `remove_class(window, selector, class_name, callback)`, `toggle_class(window, selector, class_name, force, callback)`, `set_attribute(window, selector, name, value, callback)`, `remove_attribute(window, selector, name, callback)`, `set_style_property(window, selector, name, value, callback)`, `remove_style_property(window, selector, name, callback)`, `set_form_value(window, selector, value, callback)`, `submit_form(window, selector, callback)`, `reset_form(window, selector, callback)`, `selected_text(window, callback)`, `selected_html(window, callback)`, `document_html(window, callback)`, `document_snapshot(window, callback)`, `element_snapshot(window, selector, callback)`, `capture_dom_image(window, selector, WebViewDomImageCaptureOptions::default(), callback)`, `trigger_download(window, url, filename, callback)`, `download_url(window, url, filename, callback)`, `favicons(window, callback)`, `edit_command(window, WebViewEditCommand::Copy, callback)`, `print(window)`, `clear_browsing_data(window)`, `storage_snapshot(window, callback)`, `set_storage_item(window, WebViewStorageArea::Local, key, value, callback)`, `remove_storage_item(window, WebViewStorageArea::Session, key, callback)`, and `clear_storage_area(window, area, callback)` instead of repeating raw ids. Use `element_snapshot(window, selector, callback)` to inspect one top-document hosted element before acting; it returns `Result<Option<WebViewElementSnapshot>, SharedString>` with tag, id, classes, normalized text, form state, link/src context, viewport rect, attributes, and computed display/visibility/pointer-events, and returns `Ok(None)` for no match. Use selector DOM customization helpers for app-owned hosted widgets, third-party embeds with stable selectors, visual test setup, and AI-agent customization without raw JavaScript; they return `Result<bool, SharedString>` and do not pierce cross-origin frames or shadow roots. Use `storage_snapshot(...)` plus storage mutation helpers for hosted auth/session debugging, carts, draft seeding, tests, and agent state inspection; callbacks report readable entries or browser storage errors, and origin/sandbox/quota rules still apply. Use `capture_dom_image(...)` for same-document SVG data URL previews of app-owned widgets, receipts, and agent visual artifacts; it is not a native pixel screenshot or full Electron `capturePage()` equivalent, and it does not serialize cross-origin frames, shadow roots, video/canvas/WebGL pixels, or all external resources faithfully. `print(window)` opens the native print dialog on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend. Treat WebView devtools as a debug/development aid: Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews can open, close, and report `is_devtools_open(window, callback)` state in debug/devtools builds; Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honors `.devtools()` by marking the view inspectable for Safari/Web Inspector, but WKWebView does not expose public APIs to programmatically open, close, or report inspector window state. Treat WebView downloads as supported on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; macOS `Allow` resolves to `~/Downloads` with WebKit's suggested filename, while `SaveTo(path)` must still be absolute; `trigger_download(...)` dispatches a browser `<a download>` action and returns `WebViewDownloadTriggerResult`, but browser policy, origin rules, response headers, and download handlers still decide the final destination and success. Treat WebView drag/drop hooks as supported on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; macOS forwards to WebKit when handlers return `AllowBrowserDefault` and blocks WebKit default handling when they return `BlockBrowserDefault`. Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honor `.on_document_title_changed(...)`. Use `.request_headers(headers)` on `WebViewOptions` for initial loads and `navigate_with_headers(window, url, headers)` for later navigations with `http_client::http::HeaderMap`, matching Electron `loadURL(url, { extraHeaders })` style main-frame request headers on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend; subresource requests stay controlled by the embedded browser engine. Use `url(window, callback)` for Electron-style `webContents.getURL()`; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews return the backend current URL, and Kael's custom macOS WebView backend reads `WKWebView.URL.absoluteString` with a declared-URL fallback before a page has committed. Use `evaluate_javascript_with_result(window, script, callback)` for Electron-style `executeJavaScript` value returns; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend deliver JSON string serialization through `Result<SharedString, SharedString>`. Use `cookies(window, callback)` or `cookies_for_url(window, url, callback)` for Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend session inspection; callbacks receive `Result<Vec<WebViewCookie>, SharedString>` with name, value, domain, path, secure, and http-only metadata. Use `set_cookie(window, WebViewCookie::new(name, value).domain(domain).path(path), callback)` and `delete_cookie(window, cookie, callback)` for session mutation; mutation callbacks receive `Result<(), SharedString>`. Use `clear_browsing_data(window)` for logout, account switching, demo reset, and test isolation; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WebView backend clear browser storage through their profile data stores; persistent `.storage_key(...)` / `WebViewOptions::auth_flow(...)` profiles are the cleanup boundary. General autofill control is currently a Windows/WebView2-only option and does not disable password or credit-card autofill. Browser zoom hotkeys/gestures are currently Windows/WebView2-backed; Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend handles standard Command-plus, Command-minus, Command-zero, and trackpad magnification zoom through WKWebView pageZoom; use controller `set_zoom_factor(window, factor)` for native app-owned zoom on Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend. Treat JavaScript clipboard access as a Wry-backed construction option on Linux/Windows; Kael's custom macOS WebView backend injects an opt-in native text bridge for `navigator.clipboard.readText()`, `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)`, the `text/plain` subset of `navigator.clipboard.read()`/`write(...)`, and legacy `document.execCommand("copy")`/`"cut"` text selection calls backed by NSPasteboard, while broader clipboard item MIME types remain controlled by WebKit and macOS permissions; Linux/Windows Wry-backed WebViews and Kael's custom macOS WKWebView backend honor `.media_autoplay(...)`, `.media_autoplay_enabled(...)`, `.background_color(...)`, `.transparent_background()`, `.javascript_disabled()`, and `.javascript_disabled_enabled(...)`; WKWebView clipboard behavior is controlled by macOS, page permissions, and app menu accelerators. Do not combine `.javascript_disabled()` with `.bridge_script()`, `.inject_javascript(...)`, or hosted widgets that require page JavaScript. `WebViewDownloadPolicy::SaveTo(path)` must use an absolute path. For pages you control, inject `.bridge_script()` and call `window.kael.post(kind, payload, id)` for fire-and-forget or `await window.kael.invoke(kind, payload, { timeoutMs })` for request/response. Rust receives `WebViewBridgeMessage { kind, id, payload }` and should reply with the controller helpers.
- Native media exists as primitives (`MediaSource`, `audio(source)`, `video(source)`) plus `VideoController` for metadata, play/pause/stop/seek/fast-seek, source replacement, volume/mute, loop, audio playback-rate control through `AudioHandle::set_speed`, `VideoSnapshot::ready_state`, `VideoSnapshot::buffered_ranges`, WebVTT/SRT text tracks, and `VideoEvent`s including `SourceChanged`, `Progress`, `ReadyStateChange`, `CanPlay`, `CanPlayThrough`, and `Waiting`. Prefer `VideoPlaybackPlanBuilder::url(url).content_type(content_type).webview_options(WebViewVideoOptions::default().checked()?).build_checked()?` for generated Electron-style URL video players: it validates the source, MIME/content type, WebView fallback options, returns `VideoPlaybackPlanTarget::{Native, WebViewFallback}`, exposes `can_play()`, `route()`, `controller()`, `webview_page_url()`, and `webview_element_id()`, routes HLS/DASH manifests or adaptive MIME types to browser-video fallback, and rejects memory-backed sources when WebView fallback is requested. Use `MediaSourceBuilder::file(path).require_existing_file().canonicalize_file().build_checked()?` for local video files, `MediaSourceBuilder::bytes(bytes)` / `.reader(key, open)` for non-URL sources, and raw `MediaSource::{url,file,bytes,reader}` for custom FFmpeg inputs. Query `video_capability_report()` for the honest `VideoCapabilityStatus::{Full, Partial, Roadmap}` matrix; hardware decode, native adaptive streaming, and native stream selection are Roadmap. Pitch-preserving time stretching is not implemented yet. Use `can_play_video_type(...)`, `can_play_video_source(...)`, or `VideoController::can_play_source()` for browser-style `VideoCanPlay::{No, Maybe, Probably}` confidence; use `recommended_video_playback_route(&source)`, `recommended_video_playback_route_for_type(content_type)`, or `VideoController::recommended_route()` before advanced media UI: direct files/URLs default to native playback, while HLS `.m3u8`, DASH `.mpd`, and adaptive streaming MIME types such as `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl` or `application/dash+xml` return `VideoPlaybackRoute::WebViewRecommended` until native streaming backends land; use the MIME helper for extensionless CDN URLs. For URL/file sources that need WebView fallback, call `webview_video_player_url(&source, &WebViewVideoOptions::default().checked()?)` and pass the returned data URL to `webview(id, page_url)`. `WebViewVideoOptions` supports browser-video controls/autoplay/muted/loop/playsinline/object-fit plus poster, preload (`WebViewVideoPreload`), crossorigin (`WebViewVideoCrossOrigin`), controlslist, disablePictureInPicture, initial start time, and WebVTT `<track>` tags through `WebViewVideoTextTrack` or `.webvtt_text_track(...)`; `.validate()` / `.checked()` rejects invalid poster/track URLs, controls-list tokens, text-track metadata, and unsafe object-fit values before embedding browser media. Use `VideoController::dispatch_webview_command(window, WebViewVideoCommand::...)` to drive the browser fallback from an existing controller: play/pause/toggle/stop, exact/fast seek, volume, mute, playback rate, loop, text-track selection/disablement, browser fullscreen, picture-in-picture, and snapshot requests. The fallback posts `kael-video-event` updates for playback plus selected text tracks, active cues, browser fullscreen, and picture-in-picture so `VideoPlayer` callbacks and `on_event(...)` can stay in sync with browser state. Lower-level helpers `webview_video_player_id(&source)` and `webview_video_player_command_script(WebViewVideoCommand::...)` are available when manually calling `Window::evaluate_webview_javascript(...)`. Use `VideoController::url(...)`, `.file(...)`, `.bytes(...)`, `.reader(...)`, or `.new(MediaSource::...)` for custom media control; replace media at runtime with `.set_source(...)`, `.set_url(...)`, `.set_file(...)`, `.set_bytes(...)`, or `.set_reader(...)` to reset media-derived state while preserving volume/mute/rate/loop/text-track configuration. Use `VideoPlaylist::new([MediaSource::url(...), ...]).repeat(true)` with `MediaKeyBindingBuilder::playlist(...)` for simple next/previous source replacement on hardware media keys. The controller also supports fluent setup with `.preload_metadata()`, `.volume(...)`, `.muted(...)`, `.playback_rate(...)`, `.looping(...)`, `.start_at(...)`, `.srt_text_track(...)`, `.webvtt_text_track(...)`, `.text_track(...)`, `.selected_text_track(...)`, and `.text_track_disabled()`. Read simple state with `.playback_state()`, `.current_time()` / `.current_time_secs()`, `.set_current_time(...)`, `.set_current_time_secs(...)`, `.fast_seek(...)`, `.fast_seek_secs(...)`, or `.set_position(...)`, `.duration()` / `.duration_secs()`, `.metadata()`, `.ready_state()`, `.buffered_ranges()`, `.volume_level()`, `.is_muted()` / `.muted_state()`, `.playback_rate_value()` / `.rate()`, `.is_looping()` / `.looping_enabled()`, `.text_tracks()`, `.active_text_track()`, `.selected_text_track_id()`, and `.error()`; use `.snapshot()` for aggregate state and time/cue/end event emission. Use `kael_ui::VideoPlayer::url(url, cx)` for the easiest URL-driven player; it defaults to `VideoPlayerRoute::Auto`, which renders normal URL/file media natively and automatically routes HLS/DASH browser-media manifests to a WebView-hosted `<video controls>` fallback that posts browser media events back into `VideoPlayer` callbacks and `.on_event(...)`. Call `.content_type(content_type)` on `VideoPlayer` when Auto should route an extensionless URL from a `Content-Type` header. Use `.native_playback()` to force native rendering, `.webview_fallback()` to force the browser video fallback for URL/file sources, or `.webview_options(WebViewVideoOptions::default().checked()?)` to tune the fallback page. `VideoPlayer::file(...)`, `VideoPlayer::bytes(...)`, `VideoPlayer::reader(...)`, and `VideoPlayer::source(MediaSource::...)` cover other source types. The wrapper renders active text-track cues, exposes loaded caption/subtitle tracks through its built-in controls, uses `fast_seek(...)` while scrubbing the timeline, toggles real platform fullscreen through `Window::toggle_fullscreen()` for the fullscreen button/`f` key, routes keyboard and chrome interactions through the same play/seek/volume/fullscreen callbacks, and supports attribute-style configuration with `.object_fit(...)`, `.playback_route(VideoPlayerRoute::Auto)`, `.content_type(...)`, `.preload(VideoPreload::Metadata)`, `.controls(...)`, `.autoplay()`, `.volume(...)`, `.muted(...)`, `.playback_rate(...)`, `.looping(...)`, `.start_at(...)`, `.show_captions(...)`, `.caption_style(...)`, `.srt_text_track(...)`, `.webvtt_text_track(...)`, `.text_track(...)`, `.select_text_track(...)`, and `.disable_text_track()`. Use `.on_source_changed(...)`, `.on_loaded_metadata(...)`, `.on_ready_state_change(...)`, `.on_can_play(...)`, `.on_can_play_through(...)`, `.on_waiting(...)`, `.on_progress(...)`, `.on_playing(...)`, `.on_paused(...)`, `.on_stopped(...)`, `.on_time_update(...)`, `.on_seeked(...)`, `.on_volume_changed(...)`, `.on_rate_change(...)`, `.on_loop_change(...)`, `.on_text_track_added(...)`, `.on_text_track_changed(...)`, `.on_cue_change(...)`, `.on_ended(...)`, and `.on_error(...)` for common video events; use `.on_event(...)` for the full event stream. Use `VideoPlayer::new(state)` for custom controls/state integrations.
- For custom visuals, move down the ladder: `kael_ui` component -> styled `div()` -> headless controller -> canvas/path/image/SVG/Lottie -> WebView -> custom render target/shader roadmap. Use `graphics_capability_report()` before promising Electron-style graphics parity: native styled elements/canvas/paths/gradients/SVG/Lottie are `Full`, clip shapes/effect layers/headless rendering are `Partial`, browser-only graphics are `WebView`, and public render targets/custom shaders are `Roadmap`.
- For performance claims against Electron, use matching `BenchmarkScenario` result sets, inspect `BenchmarkScenario::workload_spec()` for required metrics/interactions, and generate `ElectronComparisonReport::generate(&electron_results, kael_harness.results(), trace_file)`; do not state memory/CPU/startup wins while `report.evidence_issues` is non-empty.

## Component library (kael_ui)

Add `kael_ui = "0.3"` for 100+ shadcn-inspired components — no external component library needed. Import everything with a single `use kael_ui::prelude::*;` (do not also glob-import `kael::*`; the prelude re-exports the essentials). Initialize with `kael_ui::init(cx)` then `install_theme(cx, Theme::dark())` — 18 presets, or brand your app with `Theme::custom(ThemeTokens { primary, ..ThemeTokens::dark() })`; re-installing a theme restyles all open windows live.

- **components** — Button, Input, Select, Combobox, Checkbox, Radio, Slider, DatePicker, TimePicker, ColorPicker, OtpInput, FileUpload, TagInput, Rating, Calendar, Carousel, code Editor (tree-sitter), and more
- **display** — Table, DataTable, DataGrid, Card, Badge, Accordion, Markdown/HTML rendering
- **navigation** — Sidebar, Menu, Tabs, Breadcrumbs, Toolbar, FileTree, StatusBar
- **overlays** — Dialog, Sheet, Popover, Toast, Tooltip, ContextMenu, CommandPalette
- **charts** — line, area, bar, pie, donut, radar, gauge, heatmap, treemap, sparkline
- **layout** — VStack, HStack, Grid, ScrollContainer, responsive breakpoints
- **theme** — shadcn-style design tokens, light/dark; `Theme` is a `Global`, read it in render with `Theme::of(cx).tokens.*` (`use_theme()` is the legacy clone-per-call shim)
- Bundled: 1,600+ Lucide icons (`set_icon_base_path("assets/icons")`), Inter + JetBrains Mono fonts

## Layout (Tailwind-style on div)

`.flex()` `.flex_col()` `.flex_row()` `.gap_2()` `.items_center()` `.justify_center()` `.justify_between()`
`.w(px(N))` `.h(px(N))` `.size_full()` `.flex_1()` `.p_4()` `.px_3()` `.py_2()` `.m_4()`
`.bg(rgb(HEX))` `.text_color(rgb(HEX))` `.border_1()` `.border_color()` `.rounded_md()` `.shadow_lg()`
`.text_sm()` `.text_xl()` `.font_weight(FontWeight::BOLD)`
`.overflow_y_auto()` `.cursor_pointer()` `.opacity(0.5)` `.backdrop_blur(px(N))`
Grid: `.grid()` `.grid_cols(N)` `.grid_rows(N)` `.col_span(N)` `.row_span(N)` `.col_span_full()` `.row_span_full()`
`.when(condition, |this| this.style())` — conditional styling
`.children(iter)` — render from iterator

## Interactions on div

`.id("name")` — required for interactive divs
`.on_click(|event, window, cx| { ... })`
`.on_mouse_down(button, handler)` `.on_key_down(handler)`
`.context_menu(|menu| menu.item("Label", handler))`
`.tooltip("text")` `.tooltip_element(|| element)`

## Animations

Bring `AnimationExt` into scope, then `element.with_animation(id, animation, |el, delta| el.mutate(delta))` where `delta` is eased progress `0.0..=1.0`.
`Animation::new(Duration)` `.with_easing(fn)` `.easing(Easing)` `.delay(d)` `.repeat(Repeat)` `.repeat_forever()`
`Easing`: `Linear` `EaseIn` `EaseOut` `EaseInOut` `CubicBezier(x1,y1,x2,y2)` `Spring{stiffness,damping,mass}` `Custom(Rc<Fn>)`. `Repeat`: `Once` `Count(n)` `Forever`.
Keyframes: `Keyframes::new().at(0.0, |k| k.opacity(0.4)).at(1.0, |k| k.opacity(1.0))` + `el.with_keyframes(id, kf, anim)`.
Cancellable: `el.with_cancellable_animation(id, anim, f) -> (el, AnimationHandle)`; `handle.cancel()`.
Elastic scrolling is automatic on macOS for scroll containers; `ScrollHandle::new()` exposes `.offset()` / `.set_offset(point)` / `.max_offset()`.

## Canvas & graphics

Immediate-mode: `canvas(|bounds, win, app| { prepaint }, |bounds, state, win, app| { win.paint_quad(fill(bounds, color)); win.paint_path(path, color); })`.
Paths: `PathBuilder::fill()` or `PathBuilder::stroke(px(N))` → `.move_to(p)` `.line_to(p)` `.curve_to(to, ctrl)` `.cubic_curve_to(to, c1, c2)` `.close()` `.build()?`.
Gradients (pass to `.bg`): `linear_gradient(angle, linear_color_stop(rgb(..), 0.0), linear_color_stop(rgb(..), 1.0))`, also `radial_gradient`, `conic_gradient`, `multi_stop_linear_gradient`.
SVG: `svg().path("icon.svg").size(px(N)).text_color(rgb(..))`. Lottie: `lottie(src).autoplay().loop_forever()`.
Capability gate: `graphics_capability_report()` exposes `GraphicsCapabilityStatus::{Full, Partial, WebView, Roadmap}`. Do not tell users Kael has public native WebGL/WebGPU/custom-shader parity while `public_render_targets` or `public_custom_shaders` are `Roadmap`; use `webview(id, url)` for browser graphics islands.

## Actions & keybindings

Define: `actions!(namespace, [Save, Undo, Redo])`.
Bind once at startup: `cx.bind_keys([KeyBinding::new("cmd-s", Save, None), KeyBinding::new("tab", Tab, Some("Editor"))])` (3rd arg = optional key context).
Command registry: prefer `registry.register_action_checked("editor.save", "Save", || { ... })?` or `registry.register_checked(Box::new(command))?` for command palettes, menus, toolbars, and agent action lists; checked registration rejects empty/padded/overly long/non-portable IDs, invalid names, and duplicate IDs; raw `register(...)` / `register_action(...)` remain available for intentional replacement.
Handle: `div().track_focus(&self.focus_handle).on_action(cx.listener(Self::on_save))`, where `fn on_save(&mut self, _: &Save, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>)`.
Focus: `cx.focus_handle().tab_index(N).tab_stop(true)`; `window.focus(&h)` / `window.focus_next()` / `window.focus_prev()`.
Focus traps: for custom modals/popovers/palettes use `FocusTrapController::modal()` from `kael_ui::prelude`; in `on_key_down`, call `trap.action_for_keystroke(&event.keystroke)` and handle `FocusTrapAction::FocusNext` with `window.focus_next_in_group()`, `FocusPrevious` with `window.focus_prev_in_group()`, and `Dismiss` with the close handler. Use `FocusTrapController::persistent()` or `.dismiss_on_escape(false)` when Escape should not close.
Accessibility: for custom interactive `div()` controls prefer semantic recipes such as `AccessibilityAttributes::button(label)`, `.switch(label, on)`, `.checkbox(label, checked)`, `.link(label)`, `.slider(label, current, min, max, step)`, then call `attrs.validate()?` before `.accessibility(attrs)`; use `attrs.audit_report()` for non-throwing component reviews and `AccessibilityTree::audit_report()` before platform export when agents need all issues at once, including missing names/actions, invalid range values, conflicting states, hidden focused nodes, missing children, parent mismatches, multiple focused nodes, and unknown roles; drop to `AccessibilityAttributes::new(AccessibilityRole::...)` only for custom roles/states.
Assistive actions: advertise actions with `.action(AccessibilityAction::...)` / `.actions(...)`; normalize platform callbacks with `AccessibilityActionRequest::from_accesskit_for_node(node_id, &node, action)` or `from_accesskit_for_node_with_data(...)`, and route app handlers through `Window::on_accessibility_action(...)` or `AccessibilityActionRouter::on_action(...)` / `.dispatch(...)`. macOS/Linux adapter drains normalize pending AccessKit requests against the current tree and `Window::drain_accessibility_actions()` exposes delivered requests after platform tree updates. Windows feeds UIA focus, invoke, toggle, expand/collapse, value, and range-value pattern calls into the same window route; exact edits arrive as `AccessibilityAction::SetValue` with `AccessibilityActionPayload::Value(text)` or `AccessibilityActionPayload::NumericValue(value)`.
File drops: prefer `let filter = FileDropFilter::images().max_files(4)` / `.audio()` / `.video()` / `.media()` / `.single_file()`, then `div().can_drop_external(filter.clone()).on_external_drop(move |data, _, _| { if let Some(paths) = data.accepted_paths_by(&filter) { ... }; for url in data.urls() { ... }; if let Some(text) = data.text_value() { ... } })`; use `FileDropFilter::new().extensions([...])` for custom extension sets. Pure file drops stay as `ExternalPaths` internally for compatibility, but `on_external_drop` normalizes them to `ExternalDropData`. For custom drag bridges/tests, use `ExternalDropData::from_drag_value(value)`, `ExternalDropData::from_paths(...).with_text(...).with_url(...)`, `ExternalDropData::from_uri_list(text_uri_list)`, or `ExternalDropData::from_plain_text(text)`. macOS/Windows native text or URL drops and Linux URI-list drops emit `ExternalDropData` when non-file data is present.

## Platform APIs

Before depending on OS features, use `CapabilityReport::current()`. `report.require(PlatformFeature::WebView)?` requires full support; `report.require_available(feature)?` and `report.is_available(feature)` accept `Full`, `Partial`, or `RequiresInit`; `CapabilityCheck::new().require(...).require_available(...).prefer_available(...).evaluate(&report)` returns missing required/preferred items plus readable `required_failure_summary()` text for startup gates and fallbacks. For input-heavy apps, require `PlatformFeature::PrecisionPointerInput` and prefer-available `GestureInput`, `TouchInput`, and `PenInput`; provide mouse/keyboard controls when preferred touch/pen/gesture support is missing or partial.

| API | Usage |
|-----|-------|
| File dialog | Prefer `cx.show_open_dialog(OpenDialogBuilder::files().image_files().filter("Markdown", ["md", "markdown"]).prompt(label)).await??`, `OpenDialogBuilder::directory().multiple(true)`, and `cx.show_save_dialog(SaveDialogBuilder::new(dir).suggested_name(name).default_extension("pdf")).await??`; use `FileDialogFilter::{images,audio,video,pdf,text}()` or `.filter(name, extensions)` for open-dialog filters, and `.pdf()`, `.text()`, `.json()`, or `.default_extension(ext)` for save-name defaults; checked builders reject incoherent open modes, invalid filter names/extensions, empty/padded/control-character prompt labels, empty save directories, unsafe suggested names, and malformed default extensions; raw `prompt_for_paths(PathPromptOptions { ... })` / `prompt_for_new_path(...)` remain available |
| File drops | Prefer UI `FileDropFilter::images()/audio()/video()/media()/single_file()` for hover acceptance, then `cx.file_drop_intent_checked(FileDropIntentBuilder::media_source().paths(paths).max_paths(count).canonicalize_paths())?` or `.open_document()`, `.import_files()`, `.import_folder()`, `.project_workspace()` after drop before import/open work; checked intents validate semantic purpose, non-empty paths, file-vs-directory policy, extension allowlists, max path count, optional existence, canonicalization, and deduplication |
| File export drags | Prefer `let export = cx.file_export_drag_checked(FileExportDragIntentBuilder::generated_files(reason).virtual_file_with_mime(name, mime, bytes))?` for Electron-style file promises / drag-to-desktop generated artifacts, or `.existing_files(reason).path(path)` for dragging existing files; gate backends with `PlatformFeature::FileExportDrag`; existing-path exports require `Capability::FilesystemRead { scope: PathScope::UserSelected }`, while generated virtual files require no filesystem capability; checked intents validate purpose text, item count, safe file names, MIME type shape, non-empty generated bytes, byte limits, optional existing-path presence, and duplicate path items |
| File intake | Prefer `let intake = cx.file_intake_plan_checked(FileIntakePlanBuilder::new().paths(paths).canonicalize_paths())?` after dialogs, drops, recent docs, or file deep links; route with `paths_of_kind(FileIntakeKind::Video/Audio/Image/Project/Text/Data/Pdf/Archive/Directory)` and use `.reject_unknown()` for strict importers; checked plans validate non-empty paths, optional existence, max path count, canonicalization, deduplication, normalized extensions, and unknown-kind handling |
| Message dialog | Prefer `cx.show_message_dialog(MessageDialogBuilder::info(title, message))?`, `MessageDialogBuilder::confirm(title, message).detail(text)`, `MessageDialogBuilder::destructive_confirm(title, message, "Delete")`, `MessageDialogBuilder::save_discard_cancel(title, message)`, or `MessageDialogBuilder::error(title, message)`; use `.default_button(index)` / `.cancel_button(index)` for custom button order; checked builders reject empty, padded, control-character, duplicate, too many, and overly long generated labels; result is a button-index receiver matching the configured button order; raw `show_dialog(DialogOptions { ... })` remains available |
| Menus | Prefer `cx.set_menus_checked(MenuBarBuilder::new().menu(MenuBuilder::new(name).action(label, action).separator().submenu(...)).menu(MenuBuilder::standard_edit("Edit", undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select_all)))?` so standard Edit menus get native Undo/Redo/Cut/Copy/Paste/Select All role mappings and empty/padded/control-character/overly long labels, empty menus, and duplicate top-level menu names fail before native installation; raw `set_menus(...)`, `Vec<Menu>`, and `MenuItem::...` remain available |
| Context menu | Prefer `cx.show_context_menu_checked(position, NativeContextMenuBuilder::new().action(label, id).separator().toggle(label, checked, id).submenu(label, items), \|id, cx\| { ... })?` so empty labels/IDs, empty submenus, and duplicate action IDs are rejected before callbacks become ambiguous; raw `show_context_menu(...)` and `Vec<TrayMenuItem>` remain available |
| System tray | Prefer `cx.configure_tray_app_checked(TrayAppBuilder::new().action(label, id).separator().toggle(label, checked, id).status_tooltip(text).panel().keep_alive_without_windows(true))?` for background/tray apps so menu items, tooltip text, panel-mode click behavior, and app lifetime are validated/applied together; use `cx.set_tray_menu_checked(TrayMenuBuilder::new().action(label, id).separator().toggle(label, checked, id).submenu(label, items))?` and `cx.set_tray_tooltip_checked(TrayTooltipBuilder::status(text))?` when pieces are owned separately; checked paths reject empty labels/IDs, empty submenus, duplicate action IDs, and empty/padded/control-character/overly long tooltips; raw `set_tray_menu(...)`, `Vec<TrayMenuItem>`, `set_tray_tooltip(...)`, and `set_keep_alive_without_windows(...)` remain available |
| Clipboard | Prefer `cx.write_clipboard_text_checked(text)?` and `cx.read_clipboard_text()?` for generated/plain text; use raw `cx.write_clipboard_text(text)` only for already-validated text; prefer `cx.write_clipboard_html(plain_text, html)?` or `ClipboardItem::builder().html(plain_text, html)?` for Electron-style rich HTML with a plain-text fallback; prefer `cx.write_clipboard_item(ClipboardItem::builder().try_text_with_json_metadata(text, metadata)?.image_ref(&image))?` for rich text/image/metadata payloads when metadata may fail to serialize; checked writes reject empty items, empty text, empty metadata, empty image bytes, empty HTML, and NUL/control characters; inspect reads with `item.text()`, `item.html()`, `item.strings()`, `ClipboardString::metadata()`, `ClipboardString::html()`, `item.images()`, `item.first_image()`, `item.has_text()`, `item.has_html()`, and `item.has_image()`; raw `cx.write_clipboard_text(text)`, `cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::...)`, and `cx.read_from_clipboard()?` remain available |
| Share sheet | With the `share` feature, prefer `cx.show_share_sheet(ShareSheet::builder().subject(title).text(text).url(url).file(path).exclude(ShareType::Social)).await?` or `cx.show_share_sheet_checked(sheet).await?` for OS share/export handoff; use `ShareItem::{text,url,file,files,image}` and `ShareSheet::{text,url,file,files}` for one-line payloads; checked builders reject empty payloads, URL values without schemes, empty image MIME/bytes, and missing files before invoking platform share UI; inspect `cx.share_support()` for available destination families |
| Secure credentials | Prefer `cx.write_secure_credential(CredentialBuilder::new(service).username(account).password(secret))?.await?`, `cx.read_secure_credential_checked(CredentialServiceBuilder::new(service))?.await?`, and `cx.delete_secure_credential_checked(CredentialServiceBuilder::new(service))?.await?` for platform keychain / credential-manager storage; checked paths reject empty, padded, control-character, or overly long service/user values plus empty secrets; raw `write_credentials(...)`, `read_credentials(...)`, `delete_credentials(...)`, `read_secure_credential(...)`, and `delete_secure_credential(...)` remain available |
| Permissions | Prefer `cx.request_permissions(PermissionRequestBuilder::startup_privacy())?` for accessibility + media startup checks, `.capture_studio()` for capture/recording tools, or `.media_devices()` for microphone + camera only; inspect `requested_permissions()`, `granted_permissions()`, `pending_permissions()`, `has_pending_permission()`, `all_granted()`, `blocking_denials()`, `granted_summary()`, and `blocking_denial_summary()` before starting blocked features; use `.microphone_with_callback(...)` / `.camera_with_callback(...)` for OS prompt results |
| Shell | Prefer `cx.open_external_url(url)?`, `cx.open_path(path)?`, `cx.show_item_in_folder(path)?`, or `cx.open_shell_target(ShellTarget::...)`; use `cx.open_shell_targets(ShellTargetsBuilder::new().url(help_url).reveal_path(report_path).require_existing_paths())?` for ordered export/open/reveal workflows; use `cx.trash_request_checked(TrashRequest::builder(path).canonicalize_path())?` for Electron `shell.trashItem(...)` style move-to-trash handoffs; checked shell targets reject empty/padded URLs, unsupported shell URL schemes, missing HTTP(S) hosts, empty paths, and NUL characters; trash requests additionally reject filesystem roots, relative paths unless opted in, and missing targets by default; use `.canonicalize_paths()` when generated path/reveal targets should be normalized; shell URL targets allow `http`, `https`, and `mailto`, while custom app schemes should use deep-link registration; path/reveal/trash actions require `ShellExecute` |
| App paths | Prefer `cx.app_paths_checked(AppPathBuilder::new(app_id).all_common().create_dirs())?` for Electron `app.getPath(...)`-style data/config/cache/log/temp/download locations; inspect `data_dir()`, `config_dir()`, `cache_dir()`, `logs_dir()`, `temp_dir()`, and `downloads_dir()`; checked paths reject empty, padded, whitespace/control-character, separator-containing, and duplicate-role app path requests before storage, migrations, logs, downloads, or plugins start |
| App storage plan | Prefer `let storage = cx.app_storage_plan_checked(AppStoragePlanBuilder::new(app_id).settings_json("settings", "settings.json").sqlite_database("main-db", "state/app.sqlite").key_value_store("kv", "kv").blob_cache("assets", "assets"))?` as the native localStorage/IndexedDB/profile replacement contract; entries expose `absolute_path()`, `kind()`, `durability()`, `max_bytes()`, `is_sensitive()`, `read_capability()`, and `write_capability()`; checked plans reject duplicate ids, unsafe relative paths, parent-directory escapes, absolute paths, invalid custom kinds, Downloads as a storage base, empty plans, and invalid quotas |
| Launch context | Prefer `let launch = cx.launch_context_checked(LaunchContextBuilder::new().environment_keys([\"APP_CHANNEL\"]).require_executable().require_current_dir())?` for Electron `process.argv` / startup environment parity; `cx.launch_context()` returns a best-effort snapshot with args and no environment values; inspect `args()`, `env(key)`, `executable_path()`, `current_dir()`, `process_id()`, and `is_development_mode()`; checked launch context rejects duplicate or malformed env keys and never captures arbitrary env values unless allowlisted |

| Media keys | Prefer `MediaKeyBindingBuilder::new().video(controller.clone()).playlist(VideoPlaylist::new([MediaSource::url(...), ...]).repeat(true)).install_checked(cx)?` for simple player queues, or `.on_next_track(|cx| { ... }).on_previous_track(|cx| { ... })` for custom queues; `.audio(handle.clone())` routes hardware/OS play, pause, play-pause, and stop to audio; raw `cx.on_media_key_event(...)` remains available for custom routers |
| Network status | Prefer `let monitor = cx.watch_network_status_checked(NetworkStatusMonitorBuilder::new().on_offline(|cx| { ... }).on_online(|cx| { ... }).on_change(|status, cx| { ... }))?` for callback-driven sync/presence/offline UX; inspect `monitor.initial_status()` / `initially_online()` / `initially_offline()` for startup mode; raw `cx.network_status()` / `cx.on_network_status_change(...)` and snapshot-only `watch_network_status(...)` remain available |
| Network policy | Prefer `let policy = NetworkPolicyBuilder::new().allow_host("api.example.com").allow_url("https://cdn.example.com/app.js")?.build_checked()?` for worker/extension/sync HTTP allowlists; use `policy.check_url(url)?` before handing generated URLs to an HTTP client and `policy.hosts()` for telemetry; checked builders reject malformed hosts, full URLs in host fields, non-HTTP(S) URLs, duplicate hosts, and mixed allow/deny lists; empty builders produce `NetworkPolicy::DenyAll` |
| Session | Prefer `SessionStore::new_checked("app-id")?.save_snapshot_checked(SessionSnapshotBuilder::new().window_state("main", window.window_state()).app_data(serde_json::json!({ "workspace": workspace_id }))?)?` for Electron-style workspace restore so generated app/window IDs reject empty, padded, path-like, control-character, and overly long values, and app data rejects JSON null; use `restore_window_states(&display_ids, primary_display_id)?` after monitor changes, and raw `SessionStore::new(...)`, `save_snapshot(...)`, `SessionSnapshotBuilder::build()`, `save_window_states(...)`, and `load_window_states(...)` for compatibility or geometry-only apps |
| Displays/window placement | Prefer `cx.query_displays_checked(DisplayQueryBuilder::cursor().fallback_to_primary())?`, `DisplayQueryBuilder::primary()`, `DisplayQueryBuilder::display_id(id)`, or `DisplayQueryBuilder::all()` for Electron `screen`-style display selection; inspect `DisplaySnapshot::{id, uuid, bounds, default_bounds, refresh_rate, is_primary, contains_cursor}`; prefer `let placement = cx.resolve_window_placement(WindowPlacementBuilder::new(size(px(420.), px(320.))).bottom_right(px(16.)))?` and pass it to `WindowOptionsBuilder::placement(&placement)` so bounds and display id stay together; raw `cx.displays()`, `cx.primary_display()`, and `cx.compute_window_bounds(...)` remain available |
| Crash reports | Prefer `let mut reporter = CrashReporterBuilder::new(app_id).endpoint(url).http_client(client).build_checked()?; reporter.install_hook();` or `cx.install_crash_reporter_checked(CrashReporterBuilder::new(app_id))?` for startup hooks; checked builders reject empty, padded, path-like, control-character, overly long app IDs, relative custom report dirs, and non-HTTP(S) or hostless submission endpoints; call `submit_pending_reports().await?` on the next launch after consent; raw `CrashReporter::new(app_id)`, setters, and `install_hook()` remain available |
| Plugin crash policy | For extension/plugin hosts, prefer `CrashPolicy::validate()`, `CrashRecord::new_checked(extension_id)?`, `record_crash_checked(&policy)?`, `should_restart_checked(&policy)?`, and `next_restart_delay_checked(&policy)?` so generated restart loops reject invalid extension IDs, zero-delay loops, non-finite backoff values, and backoff factors below `1.0`; raw `CrashRecord::new(...)`, `record_crash(...)`, `should_restart(...)`, and `next_restart_delay(...)` remain available |
| Auto-launch | Prefer `let state = cx.configure_auto_launch(AutoLaunchBuilder::enable(app_id))?` or `.disable(app_id)`; builder validation rejects empty app IDs plus whitespace/control characters, and `state.app_id()` / `state.enabled()` report platform state; raw `cx.set_auto_launch(app_id, bool)?` and `cx.is_auto_launch_enabled(app_id)` remain available |
| User attention | Prefer `let request = cx.request_user_attention_checked(UserAttentionBuilder::informational().reason(reason))?; request.cancel(cx)` for dock/taskbar bounce/flash flows with generated reasons; use `UserAttentionBuilder::critical()` for urgent conditions; raw `cx.request_user_attention(AttentionType::...)`, `cx.request_user_attention_with(...)`, and `cx.cancel_user_attention()` remain available |
| Dock | Prefer `cx.set_dock_badge_checked(DockBadgeBuilder::count(count))?`, `DockBadgeBuilder::label(label)`, and `DockBadgeBuilder::clear()` for dock/taskbar badges so empty, padded, control-character, and overly long generated labels fail before platform rendering; use `cx.set_dock_menu_checked(DockMenuBuilder::new().action(label, action).separator().submenu(...))?` so empty/separator-only menus, empty submenu trees, padded labels, control characters, and overly long labels fail before native installation; prefer `cx.add_recent_documents(RecentDocumentsBuilder::new().require_existing_files().canonicalize().document(path).document(other_path))?` for OS recent-document lists when paths should be real files; raw `set_dock_badge(Some(label))`, `set_dock_badge(None)`, `set_dock_menu(items)`, and `add_recent_document(path)` remain available |
| Jump lists | Prefer `cx.update_jump_list_checked(JumpListBuilder::new().action(label, action).workspace_path(project).workspace([folder, workspace_file]))?` for Windows taskbar jump lists and recent workspace groups; use `.require_existing_paths().canonicalize()` when entries must be real paths; checked paths reject empty lists, non-action task items, empty/padded action labels, empty workspace entries, and empty paths; raw `update_jump_list(menus, entries)` remains available |
| Single instance | Prefer `match SingleInstanceBuilder::new(app_id).launch()? { SingleInstanceLaunch::Primary(instance) => { instance.on_activate(Box::new(|| { ... })); }, SingleInstanceLaunch::Duplicate { .. } => return Ok(()), }`; inspect `launch.app_id()`, `is_primary()`, `is_duplicate()`, and `notified_existing()` for startup telemetry; builder validation rejects empty, padded, control-character, path-like, and overly long app IDs before platform lock names are created; raw `SingleInstance::acquire(app_id)` and `send_activate_to_existing(app_id)?` remain available |
| Biometric | Prefer `cx.authenticate_biometric_with(BiometricAuthBuilder::unlock_vault(), \|ok\| { ... })?`, `BiometricAuthBuilder::approve_payment()`, or `BiometricAuthBuilder::new(reason)` for custom copy so empty/padded/control-character/overly long prompt reasons are rejected and unavailable devices skip prompting by default; inspect `request.status()` / `request.prompted()` for password/PIN fallback; raw `cx.biometric_status()` and `cx.authenticate_biometric(...)` remain available |
| Screen/media capture | Prefer `let manager = cx.capture_manager(); let sources = manager.sources(CaptureSourceQueryBuilder::screens_and_windows().name_contains("Display").limit(4))?; let configs = manager.configs(CaptureConfigSetBuilder::screen_with_microphone().video_frame_rate(30.0).video_resolution(1920, 1080))?` plus `CapturePipeline` for Electron `desktopCapturer`-style source catalogs and coordinated screen/mic/camera/system-audio capture; use `CaptureSourceQueryBuilder::{screens, windows, screens_and_windows, cameras, microphones, system_audio}()` for picker metadata with checked kinds, availability filtering, name filters, unavailable-source inclusion, and result limits; use `CaptureConfigSetBuilder::{screen_with_microphone, camera_with_microphone, screen_with_system_audio}()` for common grouped flows, or `CaptureConfigBuilder::{screen, window, camera, microphone, system_audio}()`, `.device_name_contains(...)`, and `.device_id(...)` for single-source/session flows; raw `CaptureConfig::new(...)`, `manager.create_session_with(...)`, `manager.devices(kind)`, `cx.is_screen_capture_supported()`, and `cx.screen_capture_sources()` remain available for platform source metadata/custom pickers |
| Settings | Prefer `SettingsStore::<AppSettings>::builder(settings_path).migration(...).load_checked()?` or `SettingsStore::new_checked(settings_path)?` for typed JSON app preferences; checked paths reject empty/control-character paths, directory targets, invalid existing parents, zero-version migrations, and duplicate migration target versions before atomic saves; raw `SettingsStore::new(...)`, `SettingsStore::load(...)`, and builder `.load()` remain available when the app owns filesystem validation |
| Undo/redo | Prefer `history.begin_transaction_checked("move selected layers")?; history.push(change); history.end_transaction_checked()?` for grouped editor/design-tool history; checked transactions reject nested begins, missing ends, empty/padded/control-character/overly long descriptions, and expose `has_open_transaction()` for cleanup; raw `begin_transaction(...)` / `end_transaction()` remain available for assert-style hand-written flows |
| Background jobs | Prefer `scheduler.schedule_with_descriptor_checked(job, JobDescriptor::new("export/video").with_priority(JobPriority::High).with_retry_policy(policy))?` or `schedule_checked(job)?` for queued worker/background work; checked scheduling rejects invalid job IDs, descriptor/job ID mismatches, self-dependencies, duplicate/invalid dependency IDs, and invalid retry policies before queue mutation; raw `schedule(...)` / `schedule_with_descriptor(...)` remain available when the app owns validation |

## Multi-process & IPC

Host: `WorkerHost::with_temp_dir()`; prefer `ProcessInfoBuilder::worker(ProcessId(0), "name").executable(path).require_existing_executable().build_checked()?` and `ProcessSpawnOptionsBuilder::new().restart_on_failure(3, duration).heartbeat_interval(duration).missed_heartbeats_before_unhealthy(3).build_checked()?`; call `host.spawn_worker_with_options(ProcessClass::Worker, info, options)?` or `host.spawn_worker(ProcessClass::Worker, info)?` for the default bounded-restart policy. Raw `ProcessInfo::worker(...).executable(path)` and `ProcessSpawnOptions::new(...)` remain available when the app owns validation. Use `worker.request(json)?` / `.health_check()?` / `.fire_and_forget(json)?`; `host.on_event(|event: SupervisorEvent| { ... })`.
Child binary: `WorkerClient::connect_from_env()?.run(|req, progress| -> Result<WorkerResponse, WorkerError> { ... })`.
Messages: `WorkerRequest::{Ping, Execute { payload }}`, `WorkerResponse::{Pong, Result(value)}`, `WorkerProgress::Update(value)`, `WorkerError::{Execution(String), Cancelled}`. Transport: Unix sockets (macOS/Linux), named pipes (Windows).

## Extensions

`ExtensionHostRuntime::new(dir, app_id)`; build with `PluginManifest::builder(id, name, version, api_version, entry_point, ExecutionModel::Wasm | ExecutionModel::ExternalProcess).command(ContributedCommand { id, title, keybinding }).build()?`; manifest validation rejects empty/padded/control-character/overly long/non-portable IDs, names, versions, and entry points, duplicate command/panel IDs, menu items referencing missing commands, and non-object settings schemas; `runtime.load(manifest)?`; `runtime.activate_with_broker(&id, &PermissionBroker::new())?`; `runtime.broadcast_notification(ExtensionNotification::SettingsChanged { key, value })`. Contribution points: commands, menu items, panels, settings schema.

## Theming

One pipeline, two cooperating types: `kael::Theme` is the serializable, file-facing theme (`colors`/`typography`/`spacing`/`radii`/`shadows`) the hot-reload watcher reloads; `kael_ui::Theme` (`variant` + rich `ThemeTokens`) is the runtime token system components render from. Flow: `theme.toml` → `kael::Theme` (Global) → `ThemeTokens` (bridge) → components.

```rust
kael_ui::init(cx);
install_theme(cx, Theme::dark()); // 18 presets, or Theme::custom(ThemeTokens { ..ThemeTokens::dark() })
install_theme_file_bridge(cx); // maps reloaded kael::Theme -> ThemeTokens, then install_theme
cx.observe_theme_file("theme.toml", |theme, cx| cx.set_global(theme))?; // file → kael::Theme → bridge → live restyle
let theme = Theme::of(cx); // read tokens: theme.tokens.background, theme.tokens.primary, ...
```

Custom mapping: register your own `cx.observe_theme_files(|core, cx| ...)` subscriber, optionally via `tokens_from_core_theme(core, base)`.

## Event pattern

All callbacks: `|data, &mut Window, &mut App/Context| { entity.update(cx, |this, cx| { this.mutate(); cx.notify(); }); }`

## Platform support

macOS (Metal), Windows (DirectX 11), Linux X11/Wayland (Vulkan/Blade)
